title: Homecoming and Scholarship
premise: Casper Hartwell, seventeen, has spent four years raising his younger siblings while his mother works hospital night shifts, treating graduation as the day his sentence ends. When history teacher Ms. Okafor pairs him with Priya Raghavan — his academic rival and the school board president's daughter — for a semester-long local history project, they uncover a decades-old land deal that quietly gutted their neighborhood's funding, buried by the very board that runs their school. As they dig deeper, Casper must choose between the safe anonymity he's built and a public fight that could cost him scholarships, while Priya risks her family's name; together they leak the evidence at the final board meeting before graduation, forcing resignations and restoring the scholarship fund their research resurrected. The book ends at graduation: Casper walks the stage not as an escapee but as someone who finally belongs to a place worth staying for.
about_author: Silas Villalobos is a former night-shift paramedic who wrote his first novel in the break room of a county hospital. He lives in a rust-belt town much like the one in this book, where he coaches debate and collects other people's family recipes.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Casper's POV opens on a chaotic morning: burnt toast, missing permission slips, little sister Nell's scraped knee, all before he catches the bus. He narrates graduation as a countdown on his wall — 141 days. The emotional beat is weary competence masking resentment he won't let himself feel.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor announces the semester capstone: pairs assigned by lottery, topic drawn from local archives. Casper draws Priya Raghavan — valedictorian track, board president's daughter, his rival since freshman year. Their first argument happens before they've left the classroom. Beat: dread sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Enemy Terms
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She resents being paired with 'the kid who glares,' but privately envies how freely Casper speaks in class. They negotiate terms like hostile nations: she handles research, he handles presentation, no socializing. Beat: grudging respect beginning to flicker under the hostility.

chapters.title: Box 47
chapters.summary: In the county archive basement, they find Box 47: sealed minutes from a 1998 board meeting about the Meridian Street properties. A librarian warns them some records were 're-homed.' Casper recognizes Meridian Street as his own block. Beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What Mom Knows
chapters.summary: Casper asks his exhausted mother about Meridian Street; she goes quiet, then admits the neighborhood once had a community trust and scholarship fund that 'just evaporated.' Priya, meanwhile, overhears her father on the phone saying the archive request was flagged. Beat: the past reaching into both houses.

chapters.title: Detention Economics
chapters.summary: Casper gets detention covering for Nell's truancy and realizes the school's discipline data skews against Meridian kids — a pattern, not an accident. He starts mapping it. Priya finds his spreadsheet accidentally shared and, instead of mocking it, adds a column. Beat: alliance forming through work, not words.

chapters.title: Dinner at the Raghavans'
chapters.summary: Priya drags Casper to a project dinner at her house. Her father, Board President Dev Raghavan, is charming until Meridian comes up; then the temperature drops ten degrees. Afterward Priya confronts him; he calls the trust matter 'settled.' Beat: love against duty begins its first fracture.

chapters.title: The Whistle
chapters.summary: A retired teacher, Mr. Okonkwo, contacts them after seeing their archive request posted publicly. He confirms the 1998 sale was illegal — trust assets diverted to a private developer with board ties. He's tried to speak before and lost his job for it. Beat: hope with a warning label.

chapters.title: Midterms and Middle Ground
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: studying together at the library, Casper admitting he almost dropped out last year, Priya admitting she chose every class to please her father. They nearly hold hands over a shared textbook and don't. Beat: tenderness arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Flagged
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor is called into the principal's office; their project topic is challenged as 'outside scope.' She defends them but is visibly warned. That night someone goes through Casper's locker. Beat: the stakes turn personal and institutional at once.

chapters.title: Nell's Question
chapters.summary: Nell asks why Casper looks scared, and whether they'll have to move again. He lies badly. Meanwhile Priya discovers her father's name on the 1998 proxy vote — not as president, but as the young lawyer who drafted the deal. Beat: guilt and protectiveness colliding.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Dev Raghavan takes Casper to lunch: full-ride recommendation letters, a quiet apartment near campus, everything Casper needs — if the project pivots to a 'safer' topic. Casper, who has never been offered anything, sits with the weight of it. Beat: temptation rendered honestly.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Casper tells Priya about the offer before she can hear it elsewhere — a choice that costs him. She's furious at her father, then at herself for doubting Casper. They commit to finishing what they started, whatever it costs. Beat: trust cemented by sacrifice.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Boxes
chapters.summary: Mr. Okonkwo hands over twenty years of documents he kept 'just in case': canceled checks, a forged signature, the developer's identity — now a state senator. They realize the story is bigger than a scholarship fund. Beat: awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Leak or Lose
chapters.summary: The board schedules an emergency vote to sell the last Meridian parcel — the lot where Casper's building stands. If it passes, his family loses their home. They have eleven days to go public. Beat: the countdown replaces the graduation countdown.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Priya's mother finds the documents and begs her to stop, invoking family, reputation, her future. Priya answers that her future is already in the file. Mother and daughter reach a raw, unfinished truce. Beat: duty and love forced to choose sides.

chapters.title: The Meridian Meeting
chapters.summary: They present to the neighborhood association in a church basement — Nell passes out flyers, Okonkwo testifies, Casper speaks about what the numbers did to real people. The room turns from skepticism to resolve. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Two days before the board meeting, Casper is suspended on fabricated plagiarism charges; Ms. Okafor is placed on leave. Priya threatens to testify anyway; her father, cornered, reveals the senator has dirt on everyone including him. Beat: darkest hour, allies scattered.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: At the packed board meeting, Priya takes the floor, names her father from the podium, and plays Okonkwo's recorded testimony. A board member breaks ranks; the vote fails 4–3. Dev Raghavan resigns that night. Beat: catharsis without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Fallout chapter: Casper's suspension reversed with apology, Okafor reinstated, a state investigation opened. Casper and Dev have one last conversation — not forgiveness, but acknowledgment. Priya moves out of the big house into a small apartment. Beat: justice as repair, not revenge.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Casper crosses the stage with 0 days left on his wall — and discovers the restored Hartwell-Meridian Scholarship bears the neighborhood's name, funded by the reclaimed trust. Nell screams his name. Priya, no longer valedictorian-track by her father's design, sits beside him as an equal. Beat: homecoming.

chapters.title: Summer, Open Door
chapters.summary: Epilogue in June: Casper tutors Nell at the kitchen table, mom sleeps in actual daylight, and Priya knocks on the door holding two archived boxes — more stories waiting. He lets her in. Beat: the sentence served becomes a life chosen.
